sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Time-Definite Small Parcel Courier Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (PRC) as the WFOE formation jurisdiction, with Taiwan, China as the investor-source jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (PRC civil-law company registration and administrative licensing; Taiwan, China investor documents governed by the cross-strait notarization/certification mechanism)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No sovereign-state BIT/DTA/FTA is applicable between China and Taiwan, China because Taiwan is not a sovereign state; the active cross-strait instruments govern:
Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion
Cross-Strait Joint Notarization and Document Verification Agreement (SEF/ARATS)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (effective Nov. 1, 2024); PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2025 revision); PRC Measures on Foreign Information Reports; State Administration for Market Regulation business registration rules; State Post Bureau international express license rules; cross-strait SEF/ARATS notarized document verification system

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Company Registration Certificate of the Taiwan, China foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization followed by SEF cross-strait certification and ARATS verification; Hague Apostille is unavailable in Taiwan, China because it is not an Apostille Convention party; PRC consular legalization does not apply to Taiwan-origin instruments. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / recent corporate status certificate of the investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) / relevant Taiwan tax agency
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notary certification in Taiwan, China, transmission of the notarial copy through SEF to ARATS for verification, then presentation of the ARATS-verified copy to PRC authorities. For documents from a Hague Apostille state, only apostille plus certified Chinese translation; for non-Apostille and non-Taiwan states, only PRC consular legalization. Do not chain apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney of the foreign investor authorizing the establishment of the CN WFOE and the execution of pre-incorporation undertakings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor board of directors; notarized by a Taiwan, China notary public where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan, China notarized board resolution and power of attorney authenticated through the SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification channel. If the investor board is located in an Apostille state, use the competent authority apostille and translation; if in non-Apostille state, use PRC consular legalization only. Never combine apostille with legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional documents) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor / Taiwan, China company registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy notarized in Taiwan, China and verified through SEF/ARATS. Parallel alternatives: Hague Apostille for Apostille-contracting states, or PRC consular legalization for non-Apostille, non-Taiwan states. The three paths are exclusive; only one applies to each document based on its origin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the investor's account conduct, KYC status, and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's issuing bank (Taiwan, China bank or other jurisdiction bank) with AML/KYC sign-off
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued by a Taiwan, China bank: notarize the bank letter in Taiwan, China, obtain SEF transmission and ARATS verification. If issued by a Hague Apostille state bank: apostille by the origin state and attach a certified Chinese translation. If issued by a non-Apostille, non-Taiwan bank: consular legalization by the PRC embassy/consulate only. The apostille and consular legalization tracks are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories, authorized agents, customers, courier franchise partners, and payment-rail beneficiaries against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated Lists; (iii) PRC MOFCOM and State Council sanctions/export-control lists; (iv) PBOC anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing lists; (v) domestic PEP databases for PRC and Taiwan, China persons, including family members and close associates; (vi) judicial, bankruptcy, tax, customs, and adverse-media watchlists. Screening must include negative news, sanctions affiliations, dual-use goods alerts, customs blacklists, beneficial-ownership mismatches, and unusual ACH Direct or Credit Card POS transaction patterns. Enhanced due diligence must be repeated at license issuance, on material ownership changes, and at least annually, with rejected transactions reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit where required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Application and Clearance Portal, administered by the provincial market regulator where the WFOE will be registered
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal enterprise name must be in simplified Chinese. It must follow the statutory four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry description + limited liability organizational form. The English or pinyin name may only be registered as a supplementary foreign-language trade name, cannot substitute for the Chinese legal name, and must be transliterated without confusion with protected words. Traditional Chinese characters and pure alphabetic names are not accepted as the statutory Chinese legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name-clearance application is rejected, the applicant may apply in writing to the same SAMR office for a review within 15 days of the rejection notice; the reviewing office must issue a decision within 15 days. If the review affirms rejection, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the superior SAMR within 60 days, or bring an administrative lawsuit before the competent people's court within six months after receiving the rejection decision. The appeal must attach the corrected four-tier Chinese name, the applicant's foreign investor registration certificate and the proposed approval basis for any sensitive token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mail-box arrangements are not permissible for this WFOE. SAMR registration, tax administration, PBOC basic deposit account opening, State Post Bureau international express licensing, and customs courier registration all require a physical, continuously occupied office and operating site matching the registered address. The postal authority will reject a license if the premises is only a virtual address, and banks will decline account opening and ACH/e-payment services where the beneficial owner cannot be site-verified. A serviced office suite with a substantive lease, company plate, and dedicated space for records, sortation, vehicles, and personnel may be acceptable; a mailbox or virtual receptionist address alone is not.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection likelihood is approximately 65% to 75% within the first 12 months after licensing. Checklist: (1) no company nameplate at the registered office; (2) no staff or responsible person available during business hours; (3) lease term shorter than one year or no original lease; (4) registered address differs from the State Post Bureau licensed operating site; (5) no on-site courier records, EDI customs logs, or financial books; (6) address is shared with unrelated entities or a virtual office. If three or more triggers are observed, inspection risk rises above 85%, with immediate licence suspension and possible refusal of the WFOE registration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) provincial registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee; Chinese enterprise registration fees were abolished; legal services are itemized separately

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: WFOE incorporation registration, business license issuance, and unified social credit code
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory registration fee in PRC for WFOE incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel for drafting Articles of Association, UBO declaration, board resolutions, and filing documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 3,500 to USD 6,000 for a straightforward WFOE with express courier license support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Taiwan, China investor document notarization, SEF certification, and ARATS verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan notary public, Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), and ARATS cross-strait verification office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee schedule plus SEF/ARATS handling and courier fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization for any non-Taiwan foreign document
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority at document origin or PRC embassy/consulate in non-Apostille state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document market benchmark for apostille/legalization and courier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of legalized foreign documents and bank reference letters
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per page plus notarization of translation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International Express Business License (postal/express license under State Post Bureau) application preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Post Bureau / provincial postal administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory application fee; law firm support is included in the legal counsel item

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PBOC basic bank account and ACH/Credit Card POS compliance onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC commercial bank / PBOC account platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published tariff for account opening, ECDI verification, and sanctions screening

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act, Articles 1, 2, 128, 129, 130, 131, 161, 172, 192, 216, 387 and 388; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4, 6 and 12; Business Registration Act and Business Tax Act; Central Bank of China (Taiwan) Foreign Exchange Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation together with Company Incorporation Application Form, Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, and CPA Capital Verification Report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Taiwan Companies Act; no statutory minimum paid-in capital and no blocked escrow account is required by law. The authorised share capital and issued shares must nevertheless be fully subscribed and the subscription consideration must be paid into a temporary bank account in the name of the company in Taiwan before incorporation registration. The adequacy of the invested amount is reviewed by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, based on the proposed cross-border express courier business plan, so the investors should set a commercially defensible paid-in capital amount supported by the remittance certificate and capital verification report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [INSERT COMPANY LTD.], A COMPANY LIMITED BY SHARES INCORPORATED UNDER THE LAWS OF TAIWAN (R.O.C.). RESOLVED, that the incorporation proceedings, the subscribers’ agreement, and the draft Articles of Incorporation of the Company filed with the Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, be and they are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved in their entirety; and that the authorised share capital of the Company be [AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] ordinary shares with par value of NT$[PAR] each, of which [ISSUED NUMBER] shares have been subscribed and shall be treated as fully paid in accordance with the capital verification report of the Company’s independent licensed public accountant, and the subscription funds are to be paid into a bank account established in the Company’s name. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be and hereby is established at [ADDRESS], Taiwan (R.O.C.), and the Chairman or any director is authorised to lease, purchase, or otherwise secure the locations of the registered office, branch offices, and operational sorting facilities, to execute leases and contracts, to make necessary zoning filings, and to advise the Ministry of Economic Affairs and municipal authorities of the registered address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following statutory officers be and hereby are appointed: [NAME] as Chairman; [NAME] as President and General Manager; [NAME] as Supervisor. The Chairman and President are jointly and severally authorised to represent the Company in all contracts, permits, customs filings, banking transactions, and regulatory applications; the Supervisor is authorised to monitor corporate governance and report to the Board. No officer shall bind the Company except in accordance with the authorization matrix approved by this Board. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [BANK NAME] is designated as the principal banking institution of the Company; that the Chairman, the President, and [NAME] are authorised to open demand, time, foreign currency, and any escrow or share-capital accounts; and that any two such authorised signatories acting together may execute payment instructions, foreign exchange transfers, and related agreements, subject to the Company’s seal policy. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorised to apply for all necessary statutory licenses, including company registration certificate, tax and business registration, express courier customs clearance registration, transport permits, environmental registrations, fire safety certifications, and any building use or warehouse permits; and to execute supplementary applications, respond to regulatory requests, and pay applicable official fees. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the First Board adopts an initial corporate governance, anti-money-laundering, and data-protection plan, that these resolutions are effective immediately, and that the Chairman or Company Secretary shall place these resolutions in the corporate minute book and provide certified copies to the competent authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval from the Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.) — online portal submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a foreign-investment application through the Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission online portal using the investor’s digital certificate or authenticated Power of Attorney. The application must describe the proposed Taiwan WFOE limited-by-shares company, the paid-in share capital, the registered office, the cross-border express courier business model, and the source-of-funds documentation. Attach the parent company’s audited financial statements for the last two fiscal years and a board investment resolution from the ultimate Chinese investor. Pay the NT$1,000 application fee and await the issuance of the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate. The certificate is a precondition for capital remittance and company registration. Any amendment of business scope or shareholding during processing must be filed before approval is granted.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form in the prescribed Investment Commission format
Power of Attorney executed by the proposed Taiwan company’s responsible person
Ultimate shareholder and parent company resolutions approving the WFOE investment
Audited financial statements of the Chinese parent for the past two fiscal years with certified English translation
Detailed cross-border express courier business plan including projected volumes, routes, and AML/CTF controls
Proposed Articles of Incorporation and list of directors and supervisors
Identity or passport copies and proof of residential address of all shareholders and officers
Investment Commission application fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a rectification query, respond within fourteen calendar days by uploading supplemental evidence or revised business plan documentation. If the application is suspended, file an application for reconsideration with the Investment Commission; if rejected, invoke the administrative appeal procedure to the Executive Yuan under the Administrative Appeal Act within thirty days of the written refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Remittance of Paid-In Capital and Temporary Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized domestic bank and the Central Bank of China (Taiwan) under the Foreign Exchange Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, the founding investor must remit the approved paid-in capital to Taiwan in the bank account of the WFOE at a licensed domestic bank. The bank will report the inward remittance to the Central Bank of China (Taiwan) under the Foreign Exchange Regulations. Provide wire instructions with precise purpose, source declarations, and the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate number. The temporary account must be designated as a share subscription deposit account and must be maintained until incorporation registration is completed and the first board resolution appoints signatories. After the funds are credited, request a bank capital certificate or letter confirming the amount and value date; this certificate will be used by the certified public accountant for the capital verification report.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Certificate
Share subscription and paid-in capital schedule
Bank account application forms and beneficial ownership declarations
Inward remittance instructions and source-of-funds statement
Power of Attorney for bank signatories and corporate resolutions
Company name reservation certificate or draft Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of deposit or capital remittance confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses or suspends the remittance under anti-money-laundering requirements, provide the corporate board resolution, updated source-of-funds statements, and a copy of the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate to the bank’s AML compliance unit. If the refusal persists, remit directly from the ultimate parent company’s bank account after updating the beneficial ownership declaration and request a compliance review by the Central Bank of China (Taiwan).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Filing with the Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company incorporation registration with the Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs. The filing is made online using the representative’s MOEA company-registration digital certificate or through an authorized notarized Power of Attorney. Upload the Articles of Incorporation, capital verification report, subscriber ledger, consents of directors and supervisors, the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, and the paid-in capital bank certificate. Register the standard business scope as International Time-Definite Small Parcel Courier Operations with secondary items of import and export trade, freight forwarding, warehousing, and customs clearance documentation. Pay the NT$1,000 statutory fee. Upon approval, the Company Registration Certificate is issued and the company acquires juridical personality for executing contracts, opening bank accounts, and applying for operating licenses.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Application Form in the MOEA prescribed format
Articles of Incorporation signed by all subscribers
Capital verification report issued by a licensed CPA
Bank deposit certificate or remittance evidence
Foreign Investment Approval Certificate
Consent and acceptance letters from directors, supervisor, and chairman
Subscriber ledger and share allocation schedule
Registered office lease contract or title deed and address proof
MOEA registration fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a suspension or query, correct the filing within fifteen days. Where the Articles conflict with the Taiwan Companies Act, submit revised Articles and a board or subscribers’ rectification resolution. If the capital verification report or paid-in capital certificate is defective, obtain a supplementary certification from the CPA and resubmit the application through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business, Tax, Labor, and Municipal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance and local municipal Department of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, the responsible person or a notarized agent must complete tax and municipal registration at the local National Taxation Bureau office and the municipal Department of Finance. This step obtains the Uniform Invoice Number and Business Registration Certificate, authorizes the use of uniform invoices and electronic receipts, and registers the company for profit-seeking enterprise income tax, business tax, and withholding obligations. At the same time, register the entity as a labor, health, and pension insurance employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration. A municipal business license for the registered office or sorting facility is required from the city or county government, including an inspection that the address is zoned for courier and logistics use.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Articles of Incorporation and uniform invoice application form
Responsible person’s identity document or passport
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for registered office and sorting center
Bank certificate and paid-in capital evidence
Tax and business registration application
Employee registration data and labor and health insurance application forms
Municipal zoning and building use checklist or certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends registration due to address mismatch or incomplete zoning proof, provide a revised lease, owner consent, or municipal use permit and resubmit. If the business scope is considered too broad for the zoning, file for temporary use approval or narrow the secondary business items in the Articles of Incorporation and tax registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Express Courier Customs Clearance, Transport, Fire Safety, and Occupational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance; Ministry of Transportation and Communications; municipal Public Works and Fire Department; local Labor Affairs Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain sectoral operating prerequisites for express courier and customs clearance. Apply for express courier customs clearance registration from the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance, if the WFOE will operate an express sortation center or perform express manifest declarations. Register as an authorized automobile transport operator or freight forwarder with the Ministry of Transportation and Communications if using in-house vehicles; alternatively submit third-party carrier agreements. If the operation includes a physical sortation warehouse, the municipal Public Works or Urban Development office must inspect the building for courier logistics use and the local Fire Department must issue a fire safety facility inspection certificate under the Fire Services Act. Obtain occupational safety clearance, civil defense and disaster prevention inspection, and any hazardous cargo handling approval from the local labor and civil defense authorities.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate and Business Registration Certificate
Articles of Incorporation with courier and logistics business scope
Express courier customs clearance application and cargo manifest or bonded warehouse plan
Customs security, AML/CTF, and data protection compliance manual
Transport vehicle registrations or third-party logistics agreements
Sortation facility floor plan, structural load engineering certificate, and fire safety approval
Occupational safety and health management plan and civil defense/disaster prevention plan
Information security policy for package data and customer records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Customs or MOTC suspends the application, remedy through a revised security manual, cargo accounting integration, or route map correction and resubmit. If the fire department identifies deficiencies, install required firefighting and alarm equipment and obtain a re-inspection certificate. If the suspension continues, file an administrative appeal to the parent ministry within thirty days of the written decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC); Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance; municipal Urban Development and Public Works Department; local Fire Department; Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Express Courier Customs Clearance Registration and Motor Vehicle Transport/Freight Forwarder Operating License, together with Fire Safety Facility Certificate and Building Use Clearance for the sorting warehouse

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Executive Yuan, Taiwan (R.O.C.)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for a standard leased urban express-courier sorting center that does not involve new land development, major waste treatment, or hazardous goods consolidation. A Category B Environmental Impact Declaration will be required if the development involves a new logistics terminal with total floor area exceeding 1,000 square meters or a development site area exceeding 1 hectare. A full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required only for major logistics parks above the Taiwan EIA Act screening thresholds or facilities receiving substantial volumes of hazardous cargo.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: domestic sanitary effluent only; if discharging to municipal sewer, comply with the local sewer ordinance and keep BOD5 below 300 mg/L, COD below 500 mg/L, and suspended solids below 300 mg/L. No regulated industrial process wastewater is anticipated. VOCs: keep total annual VOC emissions from cleaning or adhesive operations below 1.0 tonne and hourly mass emission below 0.3 kg/hr, otherwise obtain an air pollution permit. Hazardous waste: damaged lithium batteries, aerosols, and leaking chemicals must be classified under the Taiwan Waste Disposal Act, stored in labelled compatible containers for no more than six months, manifested to licensed haulers, and treated at EPA-permitted facilities. General waste sorting and resource recovery rate shall be maintained at or above 60% by weight. Noise at the facility boundary shall not exceed 70 dB(A) during nighttime operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is mandatory under the Fire Services Act and requires installation of fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, exit signage, fire alarms, and automatic extinguishing equipment where required by floor area. The local Fire Department must issue a certificate before commencement of sorting operations. Structural load inspection and certification by a licensed structural engineer is required for mezzanine floors, racking, and conveyors, with the certificate kept on site. Occupational safety clearance from the Labor Affairs Bureau covers conveyor guards, forklift operator licenses, manual lifting limits, emergency exits, first-aid kits, and fire and evacuation drills. Civil defense and disaster prevention clearance is required from the local government for the facility emergency response plan, including earthquake, fire, and hazardous material spill procedures, and must be renewed annually.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taxation Agency, Ministry of Finance (MOF), Taiwan, and the regional National Taxation Bureau (NTB); electronic portals: MOF Electronic Tax Filing and Payment Services (e-Tax Portal) and MOF Electronic Invoice Integrated Service Platform
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain registry recognition under the Company Act through the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), and, if the shareholder is mainland-of-China based, obtain the Investment Commission approval required for mainland-invested enterprises. Step 2: Before commencing business, file the statutory tax registration application with the NTB under Article 28 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act; the NTB issues the Unified Business Number/TIN and registers the WFOE as a VAT taxpayer. Step 3: For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a Taiwan fixed place of business, register online through the MOF e-Tax Portal or by appointing a Taiwan tax representative; the foreign incorporation certificate, power of attorney and service/sales contract are submitted, and the NTB assigns a withholding/TIN and, where Taiwan-source digital/e-service sales exceed the announced de minimis amount, a business-tax VAT registration. Step 4: After TIN issuance, enrol in the MOF Electronic Invoice Integrated Service Platform and set up the Electronic Uniform Invoice Turnkey/API channel before issuing invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not apply a US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch classification election; the WFOE is taxed at entity level under the Income Tax Act and the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (Taiwan Business Tax / VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a WFOE with a Taiwan fixed place of business, there is no de minimis turnover threshold: tax registration is mandatory before commencement. Small-scale Taiwan operators with average monthly taxable sales below TWD 200,000 may qualify for simplified assessed business tax at 1% instead of the standard 5% rate, but remain tax-registered; non-resident suppliers of cross-border e-services to Taiwan individuals are required to register when Taiwan-source taxable sales exceed the Ministry of Finance announced de minimis threshold currently applied in the cross-border e-service regime (TWD 480,000 per year).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates a centralized e-invoice reporting model rather than pre-approval fiscal clearance. Under Article 32 of the Business Tax Act, every taxable sale of courier/express services must be documented with a Uniform Invoice. The MOF requires active corporate taxpayers to issue Electronic Uniform Invoices (EUI/cloud invoices) and transmit the EUI XML payloads through the MOF Turnkey connection or a certified Value-Added Service Center API to the MOF Electronic Invoice Integrated Service Platform: B2C invoices are transmitted within 48 hours of issue and B2B invoices within 7 days. Each EUI contains a mandatory 8-digit random serial number, a QR code, and an encrypted message authentication code/digital stamp, allowing anti-fraud validation by the NTB in near-real time. Untimely or non-transmission is treated as failure to issue a Uniform Invoice, attracting penalties and possible administrative suspension.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, the following cross-border express courier revenue is eligible for the 0% rate: (i) export shipments where goods are covered by a Taiwan customs export entry and physically leave the territory; (ii) international transport/courier services that are directly attributable to the carriage of export goods from Taiwan to a foreign destination; and (iii) services supplied to a foreign contracting party that are used outside Taiwan and paid in foreign currency, evidenced by contract and bank foreign-exchange settlement records. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated export revenue is creditable and refundable as an excess credit. Domestic pickup, storage, sorting or final-mile delivery performed solely in Taiwan and not part of the export carriage remains taxable at 5%, so the WFOE must maintain a documented allocation between taxable Taiwan services and zero-rated export services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Taiwan Customs Export Entry (Export Declaration) bearing the customs approval number and export statistics
Carrier-issued Master Air Waybill or House Air Waybill for air express exports, or Bill of Lading for ocean/combined transport
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
Proof of delivery (POD) or overseas consignment tracking record showing receipt by the foreign consignee
Bank Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate / export proceeds collection record issued by an authorized foreign-exchange bank (Taiwan equivalent

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PBoC/SAFE regime maintains a managed floating RMB system with current-account convertibility but not full capital-account convertibility. Current-account items such as cross-border courier charges, logistics fees, and payments to overseas agents are generally settled and paid through designated domestic foreign exchange banks after the bank reviews genuine transaction documentation. Capital-account flows, including the Taiwanese shareholder equity contribution into the WFOE, shareholder loans, and subsequent profit repatriation, are separately controlled. The Taiwan-invested WFOE must complete SAFE foreign direct investment registration, open a dedicated foreign exchange capital account, and receive the equity injection through that account. Conversion of capital into RMB is permitted only on a payment-purpose basis under the SAFE 'settlement based on payment' principle; funds cannot be used for equity or securities investment or any non-operating purpose. Export and service receipts must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange settlement account; there is no mandatory conversion ratio, but retained foreign currency is subject to SAFE account quotas and bank monitoring. Profit remittance to Taiwanese shareholders is permitted only after audited financial statements are prepared, tax clearance including dividend withholding is confirmed, SAFE/FDI compliance is verified, and a lawful board resolution authorizes the dividend. The onshore remitting bank will require the correct balance-of-payments declaration purpose code and will process the outward remittance only after the full compliance file is cleared.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's Measures for Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Administration, there is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign currency receipts; 0% of export proceeds are required to be surrendered. The exporter may retain the full amount in a foreign exchange settlement account or convert to RMB as it chooses. However, all export proceeds must be repatriated to China and credited to a domestic foreign exchange account within the commercial settlement period agreed in the underlying contract. If collection exceeds 90 days from the customs declaration date, the WFOE must file a deferred export receipt collection report with SAFE through the trade credit reporting system. The receiving bank will match the incoming remittance against the export customs declaration number and the applicable SAFE trade-in-goods receipt code before crediting the proceeds to the settlement account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB basic deposit account plus SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital account and FX current account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB operating settlement account plus foreign exchange trade settlement account
Operational RMB account and foreign exchange current account supported by cross-border clearing capabilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Non-viable as a primary treasury rail in mainland China. Offshore fintech EMIs and non-bank digital banks are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE to hold WFOE deposit balances, execute foreign exchange settlement, or clear local payroll and tax payments. A Taiwan-invested WFOE in China must maintain its operational liquidity and perform all RMB and FX settlement through a licensed onshore banking institution. An offshore EMI may at most act as an auxiliary payment aggregator for international online collections if it partners with a licensed PRC payment institution, but it cannot substitute for a Tier-1 domestic clearing bank. Attempting to route WFOE operating funds through an unlicensed EMI would create an immediate AML red flag and cause the domestic bank to reject remittance onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is effectively mandatory for the initial corporate account opening. The PRC legal representative of the WFOE must attend the bank interview in person with the original corporate chop, business license, articles of association, and valid identification. For a Taiwanese shareholder, the Taiwan Compatriot Permit or passport is required; if the legal representative is not Taiwanese, a valid passport plus residence documentation is required. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally accepted by Chinese Tier-1 banks. In limited circumstances, a bank may allow a duly authorized senior officer to appear physically at the branch if the legal representative is abroad and a notarized power of attorney, board resolution, and video interview are provided, but this is discretionary and subject to enhanced KYC review. The conservative compliance approach is for the statutory legal representative to appear in person at the selected branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity in a Taiwanese-funded WFOE using layered holding companies or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry bundle for every entity in the ownership chain (articles of association, shareholder registers, certificates of incumbency), notarized passports of all natural persons with over 10% beneficial interest, signed UBO declarations, a legal entity ownership tree showing controlling interest from Taiwan to the WFOE, source-of-wealth documentation for the founding capital, and the Taiwanese corporate registration and tax reference documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between export courier charges, customs declarations, logistics movement, and incoming cross-border foreign exchange receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transport audit file consisting of airway bills and bills of lading, China customs export declarations, commercial invoices, contracts with clients and overseas agents, corresponding bank MT103 records, SAFE trade-in-goods monitoring reports, and a transaction-level reconciliation schedule mapping each foreign exchange receipt to a specific customs declaration and logistics event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions or PEP exposure obscured by shipment transshipment through Hong Kong or other high-volume regional courier hubs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: System-generated sanctions, PEP, and targeted financial screening results for all counterparties, beneficial owners, and intermediate logistics agents, an end-user and customer declaration pack, a country-of-origin and destination matrix, a written explanation of any Hong Kong intermediary arrangement, and evidence of increased monitoring procedures covering transshipment cargo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-mature capital account activity including early dividend distribution or shareholder loan repayment before operating substance is demonstrated.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CPA capital verification report, SAFE FDI registration certificate, audited financial statements covering at least one full operating cycle, tax payment records and tax clearance certificate, a board resolution approving the distribution, a debt-to-equity ratio calculation, and a written no-objection opinion from the remitting bank compliance committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwanese investor remits the equity contribution via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital account. The remittance underlying purpose must be stated as the equity capital contribution into a wholly foreign-owned enterprise under the direct investment category of the PBOC balance-of-payments classification. Both the Taiwan remitting bank and the mainland receiving bank must reference the SAFE FDI registration certificate. After receipt, the WFOE applies to convert the capital into RMB under the settlement-based-on-payment rule by submitting the underlying commercial contracts, invoices, and payment instructions; the bank will release RMB only to designated operating or construction payees. No converted RMB may be used for equity investment, securities purchase, entrusted lending, or real estate not connected to the approved business. Within 30 days of the capital injection, a licensed Chinese CPA issues a capital verification report and the report is retained by the company, the market regulator, and the bank. For day-to-day operational RMB funding, the investor can remit through a current-account settlement entry using the correct courier/logistics fee purpose code; that route avoids capital-account restrictions but still requires genuine service transaction documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to overseas courier agents, interline carriers, and logistics vendors are cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers. High-value or recurring freight obligations can be supported by Commercial Letters of Credit issued under ICC UCP 600, while documentary collections in either DP or DA form are used when the WFOE needs to exchange transport documents against payment. All outbound foreign exchange payments require the underlying contract, customs or transport evidence where applicable, the correct SAFE payment purpose code, and any necessary withholding tax clearance certificates. Domestic operating costs, payroll, and tax payments are settled through the PBOC high-value payment system and local RMB clearing channels, with same-day or T+1 settlement. The WFOE must maintain a separate tax payment account and the bank's cross-border invoice reconciliation file to prove that outbound payments correspond to real logistical services received.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts are permissible for up to 12 months where the WFOE can demonstrate a genuine courier fee receivable or payable exposure; the hedge must be on a real-demand basis and cannot be speculative.

Cross-currency swaps between CNY and USD or TWD are permissible when the notional and maturity match an underlying foreign currency loan, capital account flow, or long-term freight contract, and the transaction is filed with and governed by SAFE.
FX swaps are permissible for short-term liquidity transformation within the operating settlement cycle, subject to the bank's internal credit line and SAFE reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not permissible for onshore Chinese entities because RMB is deliverable onshore; NDF access is reserved for offshore counterparties, so the WFOE should execute a deliverable forward or cross-currency swap through its licensed onshore bank instead.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (Form 15) with audited financial statements where compulsory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau (local district tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the year immediately following the calendar fiscal year; within five months after fiscal year-end for companies with an approved special fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues from the original due date at the post-office one-year time deposit rate; late-payment penalties apply to unpaid tax; late or non-filing permits ex-officio assessment and penalties up to 3% of assessed tax for every two-month overdue period subject to a 30% maximum; persistent delinquency may trigger tax seizure, prohibitory disposition, compulsory execution, and administrative strike-off or dissolution after prolonged inactivity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders meeting approval of statutory financial statements; signed minutes and resolutions maintained in corporate registers and filed with the registration authority where director or shareholder changes are resolved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders meeting (internal corporate governance); Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) for subsequent registration updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year, namely no later than 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors are subject to administrative fines of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000 per violation for failure to convene or complete the annual approval process; continued non-compliance may cause the Ministry of Economic Affairs to order the meeting to be convened, appoint supervisors to remedy, or initiate administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report of directors, supervisors, shareholders holding more than 10% of shares, and ultimate beneficial owners required under Company Act Article 22-1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Data Bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the close of each fiscal year, i.e., by 15 January for calendar-year companies; any qualifying change in 10% shareholding, directorship, or actual control must be reported within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing triggers an MOEA correction order and fines from TWD 50,000 to TWD 500,000; repeated refusal to comply can lead to administrative cancellation of company registration or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly Business Tax Return (VAT Uniform Invoice return, Form 401/403) covering courier service receipts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 15th day of the month following each calendar quarter, i.e., 15 April, 15 July, 15 October, and 15 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a late-filing penalty of 1% of the tax payable for every two days overdue, capped at 15%, plus interest at the postal savings rate; continued defaults may lead to suspension of Uniform Invoice issuance, revocation of tax registration, and enforced business closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax and non-wage remuneration statement covering salaries, directors fees, professional service fees, and remittances paid during the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the calendar year of payment, with duplicate withholding certificates provided to employees and payees by the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of TWD 750 to TWD 7,500 per form, plus interest and recovery of short-paid withholding tax; false or incomplete forms may attract penalties up to TWD 15,000 in addition to the tax deficiency.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act Article 20, an independent audit by a certified public accountant licensed under the Taiwan Certified Public Accountant Act is mandatory for: (i) any company with paid-in capital of NT$30 million or more, approximately USD 1.0 million; (ii) any public or reporting company under the Securities and Exchange Act, regardless of size; (iii) financial, insurance, securities, futures, payment, and FinTech entities regulated by the Financial Supervisory Commission; and (iv) any company specifically ordered by the competent authority on public-interest or transparency grounds. In MOEA administrative practice, a single-year turnover threshold of NT$100 million, approximately USD 3.3 million, is treated as a relevant scale trigger for requiring audited financial statements. There is no standalone headcount trigger fixed in the Company Act; however, a workforce of 100 or more may be used as an institutional transparency indicator and may support a competent-authority order to mandate a statutory audit. The audit threshold is therefore principally capital-based, supplemented by turnover, regulatory industry status, and competent-authority designation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies must apply Taiwan IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public companies apply Taiwan Financial Accounting Standards or ROC GAAP under the Business Entity Accounting Act, with voluntary application of Taiwan IFRS permitted where the competent authority approves. Books and records must be kept in New Taiwan Dollars and Chinese, with English parallel records maintained only for offshore parent-group consolidation and audit cooperation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the company must file an annual confirmation of its directors, supervisors, shareholders holding more than 10% of shares, and ultimate beneficial owners with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 15 days after the close of the fiscal year, i.e., by 15 January for calendar-year companies. Any share transfer crossing the 10% ownership threshold, any change in actual control, and any change in directors or supervisors must be reported within 15 days of the underlying corporate event. The Register of Members must be updated contemporaneously and presented for inspection at the annual shareholders meeting. No separate annual UBO filing fee is charged by MOEA.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages (including debenture and security registers, where applicable)
Minute Book (shareholders meetings and board meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 2,500 per annum for registered office and local statutory corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to USD 8,000 per annum for a single-entity certified audit, depending on revenue volume, cross-border courier transaction count, and related-party reconciliation complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise income tax headline rate is 20%, but effective incidence is reduced by qualifying R&D investment tax credits under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, investment tax credits for automation and energy-saving logistics equipment, free-zone and free-trade-zone preferential regimes for cross-border logistics and courier operators, and exclusion or apportionment of income earned entirely outside Taiwan when performance and use occur outside Taiwan without a Taiwan permanent establishment. A 5% retained-earnings surtax applies on undistributed surplus and needs to be weighed against the 21% dividend withholding rate when planning repatriation from the Taiwan WFOE to the mainland Chinese shareholder.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 15 Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance Electronic Taxation Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return with quarterly provisional tax prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year Taiwan WFOE, the annual return must be filed no later than May 31 of the following year. For a special fiscal year, the return is due by the last day of the fifth month after the fiscal year-end. Quarterly provisional tax prepayments are due at the end of the month following each of the first three quarters, and the final balance is settled with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross service revenue derived from domestic and cross-border express courier operations, including pickup, sortation, line-haul, customs brokerage, and final-mile delivery fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan WFOE must report all Taiwan-source courier service income, including amounts invoiced to the mainland Chinese parent or to offshore consignors. Revenue cannot be excluded merely because the customer or payer is non-resident; source is determined by where the courier services are performed in Taiwan. Cross-border segments performed wholly outside Taiwan may be excluded only if supported by track-and-trace logs, airway bills, line-haul contracts, customs PODs, and allocation schedules demonstrating clearly identifiable offshore performance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Deductible Costs / Cost of Sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Labor costs, fuel, vehicle leases, airport handling fees, customs brokerage charges, line-haul capacity costs, packaging, and consumables directly attributable to courier operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically borne by the Taiwan WFOE are deductible. If the mainland parent pays Taiwan-based courier staff, leases vehicles, or settles customs charges on behalf of the WFOE, the related-party recharge must be at arm's length and documented with intercompany agreements, actual bank transfers, and tax invoices. Excessive or unsupported recharges may be recharacterized as distributions, royalties, or hidden equity contributions and will be adjusted under transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rent, management fees, information technology systems, software, route-planning licenses, trademarks, marketing, legal and tax fees, and head-office services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to the mainland Chinese parent for software, parent-brand licensing, customer database use, or management services must satisfy the arm's-length standard. Where the payment has Taiwan source, the Taiwan WFOE must withhold statutory income tax at the applicable non-resident rate; the statutory withholding rate is 20% for interest and royalties and 21% for dividends and other distributions unless an effective bilateral treaty applies. In this Taiwan/China structure, no in-force DTA currently provides relief, so statutory withholding must be complied with before the expense can be deducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains, dividend income, rental income, and gains on disposal of assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan WFOE must report interest received on intercompany loans at arm's length. If the WFOE receives royalties or Taiwan-source interest from a non-resident, the payer may be subject to Taiwan withholding at 20% unless a treaty applies. Any transfer pricing audit adjustments and deemed income from related-party transactions must also be reflected in this section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Loss Carryforward, Tax Credits and Minimum Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year net loss deduction, qualifying R&D and investment tax credits, prepaid provisional tax, and the profit-seeking enterprise alternative minimum tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan WFOE may carry forward qualified losses for ten years under current Taiwan law. The loss must be audited and recognized in the entity's Taiwan books. Free-zone logistics credits, R&D credits, and energy-saving equipment credits are claimed only by the Taiwan taxable entity and cannot be transferred to or used by the mainland parent. The alternative minimum tax may apply to certain low- or zero-tax income, including capital gains, and the final return must reconcile regular tax and minimum tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Taxable Income and Profit-Seeking Enterprise Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of adjusted taxable income after all disallowed items and deductions, application of the 20% statutory rate, subtraction of quarterly provisional payments, and calculation of the final tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE should reconcile Taiwan-source and foreign-source income with the transfer pricing documentation. Foreign-source branch income can benefit from foreign tax credits, but the credit cannot reduce Taiwan tax below the relevant minimum tax threshold. The final tax payable must be paid with the annual return, and any underpayment after quarterly prepayments will bear statutory interest and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Undistributed Surplus and Retained Earnings Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of net income, legal reserve, distribution resolutions, retained earnings, and computation of the 5% undistributed surplus surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 5% retained-earnings surtax is assessed at the Taiwan WFOE level on undistributed earnings. If the board distributes dividends to the mainland Chinese non-resident shareholder, the WFOE must withhold and remit dividend withholding tax at 21%. The director must analyze the combined cost of retaining profits at 5% versus distributing at 21%, and must ensure any deemed distribution triggered by intentionally understated earnings is also reported and subjected to withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Form No. 15 annual return triggers a tax authority demand, an additional monthly late-filing surcharge, and statutory late-payment interest. Under the Income Tax Act and Tax Collection Act, the surcharge may reach up to 10% of the assessed tax for non-filing and 2% per month for late payment, subject to statutory ceilings; intentional understatement exposes the taxpayer to civil penalties of up to three times the underpaid tax, daily interest, and criminal prosecution for fraud. If false invoices, dual books, or money-laundering instruments are used to conceal courier revenue, the Integrated Invoice Penalty Act and Money Laundering Control Act impose additional fines on both the entity and responsible directors, and the tax administration can apply departure restrictions to individuals for serious unpaid liabilities.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed by the Taiwan WFOE to a non-resident mainland Chinese shareholder, withheld under Income Tax Act
